name: City Council Regular Meeting of January 25, 2022

APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL ADJOURN REGULAR MEETING
  OF JANUARY 25, 2022

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:01 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Jessica Ancona, Mayor/Chair – present
  Alma D. Puente, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Martin R. Herrera, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present via zoom
  Dr. Maria Morales, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  WITH THE FOLLOWING EDITS/CHANGES TO THE AGENDA:

  Item 4.2 has been pulled.

  m) Mayor Ancona
  s) Dr. Morales  5-0

4.  CLOSED SESSION:

  The City Council and the various legislative bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council will attempt to address and complete all
  Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. If the City Council completes
  all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the City Council will take a short recess
  and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m. In the event the City
  Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed Session items by 7:00
  p.m., the City Council will hear all such remaining items toward the end of the meeting,
  immediately following Council Communications. Should any member of the public wish
  to address the City Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the City Council
  shall allow such person to address the City Council on such matter(s) prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an agendized
  Closed Session matter shall (i) call-in at the number indicated on page 1 of this agenda,
  above, prior to the City Council going into closed session; and (ii) be subject to a single
  speaker time allotment of 3 continuous minutes total per speaker to address the City
  Council on any or all closed session items of business.

  Mayor Ancona invited members of the public to address the City Council on Closed
  Session Items 4.1 and 4.3. Item 4.2 was pulled.

  Mayor Ancona and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at approximately
  6:03 p.m. Mayor Ancona and the City Council reconvened from Closed Session at
  approximately 7:01 p.m.

  Assistant City Attorney Richard Padilla reported out of Closed Session with respect
  to Items 4.1 and 4.3.

  4.1  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2) and
  54956.9(e)(1) – Conference with Legal Counsel – Anticipated Litigation – One (1)
  Matter.

  General update was provided, feedback given by the City Council but no final
  action taken.
   City Council Adjourn Meeting Minutes of January 25, 2022

  4.2  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1) –
  Conference with Legal Counsel – Existing Litigation – City of El Monte vs. Regency
  Outdoor Advertising, Inc., et al., LASC Case No. 21PSCV00565.

  Item was pulled.

  4.3  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6 – Conference with
  Labor Negotiators.

  Bargaining Units Subject to Negotiations: El Monte General Unit (SEIU Local
  721); El Monte General Mid-Management Unit (SEIU Local 721); El Monte Police
  Officers Association; El Monte Police Mid-Manager’s Association; and All
  Unrepresented Employees of City Executive Team.

  City’s Designated Negotiator: Alma K. Martinez, City Manager and John Nguyen,
  Human Resources/Risk Management Director.

  General update was provided, feedback given by the City Council, but no
  final action taken.

  OPEN SESSION PROCEEDINGS

(Commencing at 7:00 p.m. or as soon thereafter as the City Council reconvene from Closed
Session/Short Recess).

5.  INVOCATION:  City Council. Mayor Pro Tem Puente.

6.  FLAG SALUTE:  City Council. Mayor Ancona.

7.  RECOGNITIONS, HONORS AND COMMUNITY INTEREST PRESENTATIONS: None

8.  GENERAL PUBLIC COMMENT:

  This time has been set aside for members of the public to directly address the City Council
  on agendized items of business (other than those agendized as public hearing or closed
  session items) or on any other item of interest to the speaker that is within the subject
  matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing Authority, the Financing Authority
  and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”). Each speaker will be limited to a
  single allotment of three (3) continuous minutes total to address the Council on any or all
  matters covered by this section. As explained more specifically under the Public Hearing
  portion of this agenda, members of the public wishing to offer comment on items of
  business agendized under the Public Hearing portion of the agenda shall have a separate
  allotment of three (3) continuous minutes per speaker per public hearing item. Except as
  otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.), the Council
  may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted agenda but
  may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent meeting. The
  Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for consideration at a future
  meeting. Persons wishing to address the Council on matters covered under General
  Public Comment shall call in at the number indicated on page 1 of this agenda, above, by
  or before the General Public Comment portion of the agenda is closed. As indicated,
  above, the Council shall be under no obligation to entertain comments from caller wishing
  to address matters covered under this section after the General Public Comment portion
  of the agenda is closed.

  Biden – [INAUDIBLE]

9.  CITY TREASURER’S REPORT: None

  2
   City Council Adjourn Meeting Minutes of January 25, 2022

10.  DEMAND RESOLUTION NO. D-657

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF EL MONTE, CALIFORNIA,
  ALLOWING CERTAIN CLAIMS AND DEMANDS AND SPECIFYING THE FUNDS OUT
  OF WHICH THE SAME ARE TO BE PAID.

  THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF EL MONTE, CALIFORNIA, DOES RESOLVE AS
  FOLLOWS: SECTION 1. That the attached list of claims and demands totaling
  $8,609,072.81 have been examined by the City Treasurer and that warrant numbers
  1103227 through 1103650, and the payroll period December 16, 2021 through December
  31, 2021 inclusive are hereby allowed in the amounts and ordered paid out of the
  respective funds as set forth.

  m) Mayor Pro Tem Puente
  s) Councilmember Herrera  5-0

11.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES: None

12.  CONSENT CALENDAR:

  All matters listed under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine in nature and
  may be enacted by one motion approving the recommendation listed on the Agenda. One
  or more items may be removed from the Consent Calendar so that they may be discussed,
  considered, and voted upon individually by the Council. A matter may be removed from
  the Consent Calendar and taken up separately by way of a seconded motion of any
  member of the Council with the approval of a majority of the Council quorum.

  12.1  Waiver of Full Reading of Ordinance(s).

  RECOMMENDATION OF BUSINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

13.  PUBLIC HEARINGS:

  Members of the public wishing to address the Council on any item of business agendized

  City Council shall be under no obligation to entertain comments from speakers who call in
  after the public comment portion of the public hearing matter they wish to speak on has

   City Council Adjourn Meeting Minutes of January 25, 2022

18.  COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS/REPORTS:

  18A.  Mayor Ancona

  18B.  Mayor Pro Tem Puente

  18B.1 Discussion Regarding Transitional Module Housing.

  Mayor Pro Tem Puente – Asked about status of the discussion regarding
  transitional module housing.

  City Manager – Spoke about an RFP being put together to locate available sites.
  Will finalize the Homekey Project and will bring this item back to the Council for
  further discussion and consideration by the City Council.

  Mayor Pro Tem Puente – Requested information regarding funding sources for this
  item.

  Mayor Ancona – Asked direction was given to move forward with an RFP or was
  the request was just for more information like potential sites, how much this will
  cost, potential funding sources.

  City Manager Martinez – Explained that when staff brings the RFP before the City
  Council it will be to ask the Council for either: direction moving forward with the
  RFP; also options on best practices different projects.

  Mayor Pro Tem Puente– How soon do you think we will be hearing back from staff?

  City Manager – First meeting in March. This will be a presentation.

  18B.2 Update Regarding Universal Income.

  Mayor Pro Tem Puente – How are we doing with Universal Income conversation.

  City Manager Martinez – Informed the Council that this will be brought to the next
  City Council meeting.

  18C.  Councilman Herrera

  Thanked the employees for doing a great job during the holidays, participating in
  the giveaways to families in need. Also thanked the volunteers too and the Police
  Department. The officers who worked with him over the holidays they were able
  to identify some families in the community and I appreciate you in enabling that for
  me. It was heartwarming to see the connection you guys have with the community.

  Recently we were participants at the celebration for the Swat Team it was their 25th
  anniversary. Asked the City Manager if something could be done in the near future
  to recognize the 25th anniversary of the Swat Team at a Council meeting.

  CM Martinez – We will do a Council recognition, when would you like that?

  Mayor Ancona – Expressed her concern since the City is closed to the public. She
  would like to recognize the Swat Teams 25th anniversary just wants to make sure
  it is just being equitable to all employees who want to attend the meeting.

  Councilmember Herrera – Maybe the 2nd meeting in February.

  18D.  Councilwoman Martinez Muela

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – Asked the CM Martinez if she will be presenting
  the Guaranteed Income item. She would like to hear on some of the research that
  was done.

  CM Martinez – I am happy to share my research it is mainly based on the Census
  Data and most needy population.

  6
   City Council Adjourn Meeting Minutes of January 25, 2022

  Councilmember Martinez Muela had questions regarding Street Vendors
  populating on Garvey and Peck Road. Informed the Council about conversations
  she’s had with business owners who have stated that these vendors have been
  leaving trash on their properties including using local businesses trash bins.

  Councilmember Herrera – Explained that City staff and the Ad Hoc committee
  continue to have meetings and they do realize that there are some issues that are
  ongoing. The City is working with some property management to address some of
  those situations for the issue as a whole we continue to do enforcement.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – Maybe this is the time to maximize the Go
  Request app so we can hear from these local businesses to get data regarding
  some of the issues that we have been having.

  18D.1 Discussion on Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Policies Supporting EMPD,
  Administration and Staff.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – Asked the City Manager what she could share
  with the Council with regards to diversity, equity and inclusion for our Police
  Department and employees throughout the organization.

  CM Martinez – Informed the Council that she is working on a comprehensive plan
  to bring to the Council for consideration and review. She is currently working with
  the City Attorney and HR. Your questions were very specific to specific
  department, and we want to make sure it is a blanket policy that will benefit all of
  the employees.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – Expressed that her Council communication
  incorporates the entirety of the administration where are the HR policies when it
  comes to diversity, equity, and inclusion when it comes to promotions, with regards
  to leadership positions and are they reflected of our community.

  City Attorney Olivarez – The City Attorney’s Office is currently working with City
  staff on producing these policies for the City Council to review and vet. There are
  some legal issues associated with policies like this. Staff wants to make sure that
  whatever we bring before the City Council doesn’t put the City in a bad position
  from a legal standpoint. Additional time is needed to be able to bring this to the
  City Council.

  Councilmember Martinez – Looks forward to seeing something the first meeting in
  March. DEI policies are corporatewide, industrywide.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – Would also like to talk about City Sponsored
  Events 2022, when will that be?

  CM Martinez – City staff is going to put together a budget as well as something for
  Council consideration around the time of midyear budget.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – Just wanted to make sure that this is part of the
  midyear budget conversation. Thank you to staff for keeping our City moving.

18E.  Councilwoman Dr. Morales

  Want to highlight to staff that the White House has just recently released a fact
  sheet for the competitive infrastructure funding opportunities for local
  governments. Some of their funding sources are going to be available now as the
  first quarter 2022 including infrastructure and sustainability and equitable grants
  around transportation so given the fact that we have several projects going on in
  the City that were not funded in the past perhaps we can use some of those
  projects identified before and apply for those again.

  18E.1 Discussion on Community Based Policing and Crime Statistics/Updates.

  Dr. Morales – Wanted to ask Interim Chief Lowry Wanted to ask Interim
  Chief Lowry in regard to crime statistics and information on local newscast.

  7
   City Council Adjourn Meeting Minutes of January 25, 2022

  Knows these are different times covid has created challenges that we could
  of never expected. I know our crime rates were decreasing but I am
  wondering if you could share some of the crime data that is available to us
  here in El Monte and kind of get us into what the plan moving forward will
  be.

  Acting Chief Lowry – Provided updates and information to the City Council.

At 9:57 p.m.

  Mayor Pro Tem Puente – One of the thoughts that I had as I am thinking of
  my one-year anniversary here is to ask staff and see if there is support from
  my colleagues figuring out a way and putting an end cap on this cannabis
  issue. What have other cities done in order to make sure that our City is no
  longer open to new litigation in this realm make sure that we are protecting
  the City.

  City Attorney Olivarez – City Attorney’s Office can do a presentation at the
  next meeting and layout some actions of some of the things that you can
  do so that the community knows, right now there are six licenses, we can
  make it clear to the community that you want to cap at that number so we
  can do a resolution a moratorium. If you give me until the next meeting we
  can lay out what those options are.

  Mayor Pro Tem Puente – That is what I am looking for and I hope there is
  support from this body of that issue and the openness of what the City
  Attorney can bring in regard to this.

  Mayor Ancona – There is a cap on dispensaries that is a done deal unless
  it goes back to the voters in regard to all other cannabis operations that is
  at the will of the Council I am on board with you in bringing something
  forward to putting a cap.

  City Attorney Olivarez – There are other things that can be done to let the
  community know

  8
   City Council Adjourn Meeting Minutes of January 25, 2022

19.  ADJOURNMENT:

  m) Mayor Ancona

  The next Regular Meeting of the City Council will be held on February 1, 2022 at 6:00

  physically posted no less than 72 hours prior to the start of the subject regular meeting.
  Although it is the City’s practice and desire to electronically post a copy of this Agenda
  along with supporting material as part of its website posting, the size or formatting of
  certain supporting materials may render their website posting infeasible. Nevertheless, all
  supporting materials related to any item on this Agenda, that is made available to the
  members of the council may be inspected by members of the public at the City Clerk’s
  Office located at 11333 Valley Boulevard, El Monte, Monday through Thursday, 7:00 am
  – 5:30 pm. For more information, please call the City Clerk’s Office at 626-580-2016.

  All public meetings and events sponsored or conducted by the City of El Monte are held
  in sites accessible to persons with disabilities. Requests for accommodations may be
  made by calling the office of the City Clerk at (626) 580-2016 at least three (3) working
  days prior to the event, if possible. This Agenda and copies of documents distributed at
  the meeting are available in alternative formats upon request.
